title: Future predictions
function: Make predictions and talk about the future

sections.heading: Will for predictions
sections.body: 'Will' is used to make predictions about the future. It is also used for promises, offers and instant decisions. It does not change form.

sections.heading: Form
table: I / You / He / She / It / We / They
She won't come to the party.

sections.heading: Will vs Going to
sections.body: Use 'will' for predictions based on opinion or belief. Use 'going to' for predictions based on evidence.
table: I think it will rain tomorrow.
Look at those clouds! It's going to rain.

sections.heading: Common uses of will
list: Predictions: I think she will pass the exam.
Promises: I will call you tomorrow.
Offers: I will help you with your bags.
Instant decisions: I will have the soup, please.
Facts about the future: The sun will rise at 6 am.

sections.heading: Time expressions
list: tomorrow, the day after tomorrow
next week, next month, next year
in 2050, in the future, soon
I think... / I don't think... / Maybe...

sections.heading: Common mistakes
list: Do not use 'will' with 'to': 'I will to go' is wrong. Say 'I will go'.
Do not add -s to 'will': 'She wills come' is wrong.
Do not confuse 'will' (opinion prediction) with 'going to' (evidence).

phases.name: Discovery
phases.intro: Look at these sentences. Read them carefully and think about the questions below.
sentences: I think it will rain tomorrow.
Look at those clouds! It's going to rain.
She will be a famous singer one day.
I will help you with your homework.
Will you come to my party?
I won't be at home tonight.
I promise I will call you later.
Maybe we will travel to Spain next year.
questions: In sentences 1 and 2, what is the difference between 'will' and 'going to'?
In sentence 3, why can we use 'will' for a prediction?
In sentence 4, what use of 'will' is it (prediction, offer, promise)?
In sentence 5, how do we make a question with 'will'?
In sentence 6, how do we make the negative?
In sentence 7, what use of 'will' is it (prediction, offer, promise)?

questions.prompt: I think it ___ rain tomorrow.
She ___ come to the party. She has other plans.
___ you help me with this?
Look at those clouds! It ___ rain.
questions.explanation: Based on evidence we use 'going to'.

questions.prompt: I promise I ___ call you tomorrow.
I ___ have the soup, please.
Maybe we ___ travel to Italy next summer.
I don't think it ___ snow tomorrow.
She ___ probably arrive late.
They ___ win the match. They are the best team.

phases.name: Free practice
prompts: Write 5 predictions about your life in 10 years using 'will'.
Write 5 predictions about the weather for this week using 'will' and 'going to'.
Write 5 sentences about your plans for next weekend. Use 'will' for decisions and 'going to' for plans.

sections.heading: Key rules
list: Will + base verb for predictions, promises and offers.
Won't = will not (negative).
Question: Will + subject + verb?
Will for opinion predictions; going to for evidence-based predictions.
Will does not change form (no -s with he/she/it).

sections.heading: Common mistakes
list: Do not use 'to' after 'will': 'I will to go' is wrong.
Do not add -s to 'will': 'She wills come' is wrong.
Do not confuse 'will' with 'going to'.

sections.heading: Useful phrases
list: I think it will...
I don't think she will...
Will you...?
I won't...
I promise I will...
Maybe we will...
She will probably...
